newsitem.title: FRANCE: France defends Himalayas hunt for magistrate.
newsitem.headline: France defends Himalayas hunt for magistrate.

text.p: The French government acknowledged on Tuesday it had tried to track down a magistrate trekking in the Himalayas to discuss a probe against the wife of Paris mayor Jean Tiberi, but said it was to comply with judicial rules.

The unsuccessful helicopter search for prosecutor Laurent Davenas in Nepal, disclosed earlier this month by the satirical weekly Le Canard Enchaine, sparked a scandal and charges that the government was trying to block an embarrassing probe.
Tiberi, a long-serving deputy to Jacques Chirac when he was mayor of the capital, succeeded to the post after Chirac won the presidency in May 1995.

Questioned in the National Assembly, Justice Minister Jacques Toubon said it had been legally necessary to check with Davenas that the probe ordered in his absence by his deputy Hubert Dujardin did not contradict his instructions.
"We had to check it out," Toubon said.

The helicopter chartered by the French embassy in Kathmandu failed to find Davenas and the probe is going ahead into suspicions that Tiberi's wife Xaviere was paid from public funds for work she did not perform.

Dujardin has since said he took advantage of his superior's absence to launch the probe, as he was legally entitled to do, since the two men disagreed on the seriousness of the charges and he believed Davenas would fail to act.

The probe is to examine a report written by Xaviere Tiberi to verify her claim that she produced it in return for the sum of 200,000 francs ($40,000) paid her by the elected council of the Essonne region, near Paris.
The report was found during a search of the Tiberis' home by investigating magistrate Eric Halphen, who is probing the finances of the ruling RPR party, founded by Chirac.
